title: Volumetric super-resolution imaging by serial ultrasectioning and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy in mouse neural tissue
protocol: Euthanize mouse.
Enucleate eyes.
Dissect retinae in room temperature 1× PBS.
Fix dissected tissue in room temperature 4% PFA for 10 min to 1 hour.
Wash retinae in 1× PBS for 2× 20 min.
Place washed retinae in a clean petri dish filled with room temperature 1× PBS.
Punch out a 500 μm diameter region of interest using a 25G blunt ended needle under stereoscope guidance.
Transfer the punched-out tissue to a 24-well plate and incubate in blocking buffer for 3–4 h at room temperature with constant agitation.
Prepare primary antibody solution by diluting 1 mg/mL antibody stocks to 1:100 in blocking buffer.
Transfer tissue punches to a new well containing primary antibody solution.
Incubate at 4°C for 48–72 h with constant agitation.
Transfer tissue to a new well containing wash buffer.
Incubate at room temperature for 6 × 20 min washes with constant agitation.
Prepare secondary antibody solution by diluting secondary antibody conjugate stocks to 1:100 in blocking buffer.
Transfer tissue punches to a new well containing secondary antibody solution.
Incubate for 24 h at 4°C with constant agitation, protecting samples from light.
Transfer tissue to a new well containing wash buffer.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 × 20 min washes with constant agitation, protecting samples from light.
Dilute WGA conjugate stock 1:10 in 1× PBS.
Transfer tissue to a new well containing WGA solution.
Incubate at room temperature for 12–16 hours with constant agitation, protecting samples from light.
Transfer tissue to a new well containing 1× PBS.
Incubate at room temperature for two 20-minute washes with constant agitation, protecting samples from light.
Coat the inside of the pipette tip with blocking solution before transferring tissue punches.
Transfer tissue to a new well containing post-fixation solution (3% PFA, 0.1% GA).
Incubate for 2 hours with constant agitation, protecting samples from light.
Transfer tissue to a new well containing 1× PBS.
Incubate at room temperature for two 20-minute washes with constant agitation, protecting samples from light.
Dehydrate and embed samples in resin.
Transfer tissue into a clean Eppendorf tube and immerse in a 50% EtOH solution (100% EtOH diluted in ddH2O).
Incubate the tissue at room temperature for 20 min with constant agitation and protect from light.
Repeat the dehydration process with 70%, 90%, 100%, and another 100% EtOH solutions, incubating each for 20 min.
Transfer the tissue into a clean Eppendorf tube and immerse in a solution containing 2 parts 100% EtOH to 1 part resin.
Incubate at room temperature for 2 h with constant agitation and protect from light.

Repeat the resin infusion process with 1:1 EtOH:resin, then 1:2 EtOH:resin, followed by 100% resin twice, incubating each step for 2 h except for overnight pause if necessary in 1:2 EtOH:resin or 100% resin.
Transfer individual tissue punches into lids of embedding (Beem) capsules and gently center them under stereoscope guidance.
Fit the capsule body onto the lid and fill with 100% resin.
Incubate samples at 70°C for 16 h.
Trim and cut resin to produce 70 nm-thick serial section ribbons.
Expand sections using chloroform vapor.
Secure gelatin coated coverslip in plastic forceps.
Guide the coverslip into the histo Jumbo diamond knife water bath.
Use an eyelash tool to guide sections onto the middle of the coverslip.
Slowly retract the coverslip from the water bath by turning the knob on the micromanipulator.
Warm coverslips with sections facing upward on a hot plate set to 60°C for 20 min.
Immerse the coverslip in 10% sodium ethoxide for 5 min.
Wash the coverslip with 95% EtOH for approximately 30 seconds.
Wash the coverslip by immersing it in filtered H2O.
Dry the coverslip using compressed/forced air.
Mix 1 μL of bead stock with 9 μL of 1× Dulbecco's PBS (DPBS) to make a high density bead solution.
Apply a small droplet (∼1 μL) of the high density bead solution to the coverslip.
Add 750 μL DPBS to the dense bead working stock and vortex for a low density bead solution.
Apply a small droplet (∼1 μL) of the low density bead solution to the coverslip.
Wash the coverslip using filtered H2O for approximately 1 minute.
Dry the coverslip using forced air.
Place the dry coverslip tissue-side-down onto the slide with double-sided tape.
Use a pipette tip to apply pressure on the tape sides to seal the coverslip to the adhesive.
Prepare STORM imaging buffer and mix by gentle pipetting.
Draw up 160 μL of the STORM buffer into a pipette and slowly release it in the space between the coverslip and slide.
Apply a strip of epoxy to all sides of the coverslip (short sides first) to seal the imaging chamber.
Place the preparation in a dark place to dry for approximately 5 minutes.
Test that the epoxy created a seal around the imaging chamber by applying gentle pressure with a pipette tip to the surface of the coverslip.
Patch any hole using more, freshly mixed epoxy if buffer leaks are observed.
Apply a single strip of double-sided tape onto the short sides of the slide and trim off overhangs with a razor blade.
The preparation is ready for imaging.
Install "storm_control" v2019.06.28 on the local acquisition computer.
Use hal4000.py to control the microscope stage, laser illumination, focus lock, emission filter wheel, and sCMOS camera.
Operate steve.py for image tiling and ROI selection during automated imaging.
Control dave.py as master software to pass instructions to hal4000.py based on ROIs set using steve.py.
Move to the final section of the protocol paper after completing STORM and conventional image acquisition.
Collect conventional images of all color channels in rapid succession for the ROI(s) in each physical section of the sample.
Collect STORM movies for ROI(s) across all physical sections.
Image red emitters (DY-749P1/Alexa647) first within each ROI across the entire sample.
Image Cy3B and Atto488 emitters sequentially for each ROI in a second image pass across the sample.
Collect fiducial marker images for chromatic aberration correction in conventional and STORM images.
Power on the microscope and lasers.
Clean the oil immersion objective.
Apply 2–3 drops of 100% methanol to a folded piece of lens paper and gently wipe the surface of the objective.
Rotate the turret to position the 4× objective in the light path.
Secure the imaging chamber in the stage holder.
Use a top-side clamping stage insert or double-sided tape applied to the glass slide to secure the specimen in the stage.
Launch hal4000.py acquisition software.
Load settings .xml files by dragging and dropping settings files into the main Hal interface.
Engage the low magnification array setting in Hal.
Use the ‘Illumination’ control panel to engage the 561 nm laser, locate the bead fields on the coverslip and focus the objective.
Use the ‘Stage Control’ panel to zero the stage position.
Create a low-magnification mosaic of the bead fields and sample (serial sections).
Launch ‘Steve.py’ software.
Place cursor at or near the 0, 0 coordinates and press the spacebar to take an image.
Click on an ROI and press the spacebar to take an image in manual imaging mode.
Click on an ROI and press keypad #3 for automated 3×3 image tiling in semi-automated mode.
Press the spacebar to interrupt the sequence in semi-automated mode.
Adjust laser output power empirically to maximize the image intensity without saturating the image.
Navigate the sample view by right-clicking on an ROI and selecting “Go to Position”.
Finish mosaic and save.
Adjust the stage position back to the sparse bead field.
Lower the 4× objective away from the sample by turning the focus knob on the microscope.
Rotate the turret to position the oil-immersion objective in the light path.
Place a droplet of immersion oil on the objective.
Focus on the sparse beads.
Engage the high magnification array setting in Hal.
Turn on a visible imaging laser (488 nm or 561 nm) using the illumination control panel in Hal.
Bring the sample into focus.
Use the ‘Focus lock’ control panel to lock the focal plane.
Set TIRF angle to maximize signal-to-noise at low illumination power.
Reimage selected regions of the low magnification mosaic at high magnification.
Adjust the mosaic positions within the ‘Objective Settings’ panel to correct offsets between low and high magnification.
Select sample ROIs for automated imaging using a mouse cursor.
Hover over an ROI in the first physical section with the mouse cursor.
Right click and select ‘Record position’.
Repeat for each ROI across all serial sections.
Click ‘File’ and ‘Save positions’ to save a ‘positions.txt’ file when all positions are selected.
Delete all recorded positions in Steve.
Select ROIs in sequential order of physical sectioning to simplify downstream alignment processing.

Select the order of ROIs to begin imaging the end of the sample ribbon at the furthest end of the coverslip in the direction of the TIRF beam to prevent unwanted bleaching during acquisition of serial section images.
Use a mouse cursor to hover over ROIs in bead fields for automated imaging.
Record position within a region away from the edge of the bead spot in the sparse bead field.
Move cursor to a new position within the bead spot (away from the edge and the first position), right click, and select ‘Record position’.
Move cursor to the center region of the dense bead field, right click, and select ‘Record position’.
Click ‘File’ and ‘Save positions’ to save a ‘bead_positions.txt’ file.
Engage the ‘Conv’ setting in Hal for conventional image acquisition settings.
Focus on a representative ROI within the sample.
Adjust laser powers using the illumination control panel for each channel to be imaged, ensuring images are not dim/saturated.
Avoid saturating dense bead images and ensure sufficient illumination intensity to use the full dynamic range of the camera.
Engage the ‘Regbeads’ setting in Hal for sparse bead field image acquisition settings.
Focus on a representative ROI within the sparse bead field.
Adjust 750 nm laser power using the illumination control panel to visualize IR beads in the 750 and 647 channels.
Adjust 488 nm laser power using the illumination control panel to visualize visible beads in the 647, 561, and 488 nm channels.
Avoid saturating sparse bead images.
Prepare illumination power settings for dense bead field image acquisition.
Engage the ‘FFCbeads’ setting in Hal.
Focus on a representative ROI within the dense bead field.
Adjust 750/647/561/488 nm imaging laser powers using the illumination control panel to visualize dense beads.
Avoid saturating dense bead images.
Ensure sufficient illumination intensity to use the full dynamic range of the camera.
Prepare illumination power settings for STORM image acquisition.
Engage the ‘750STORM’ setting in Hal.
Focus on a representative ROI within the sample.
Using the illumination control panel, adjust the 750 nm laser power to maximum and the 405 nm laser to minimum.
Change the directory filename to ‘750storm’ in Hal.
Set the working directory to ‘Acquisition\create_xml\powertest\'.
Set 'Mode’ to ‘Run_til_abort’.
Click ‘Record’ to begin manual STORM movie acquisition.
Manually ramp 405 nm laser power using the illumination control panel to reactivate fluorophore switching to maintain optimal emitter density.
Pressing 'Stop’ ends the movie recording and saves the power progression file.
Repeat steps for 647 nm, 561 nm, and 488 nm STORM movies.
Change directory filenames according to wavelength using the specified format.
Set working directory in Hal interface to local storage drive.
Ensure local storage drive has sufficient capacity for image acquisition.
Adjust imaging parameters (e.g., number of frames, frame rate) for multi-channel acquisition in a ‘master.xml’ file.
Launch ‘Master_xml_generator.py’.
Select desired ‘master.xml’ file containing imaging parameters.
Change file name and save out final ‘master_run.xml’ file.
Launch ‘Dave.py’ software.
Click ‘File/load’ and select the ‘master_run.xml’ file for automated imaging.
Click ‘Validate’ to confirm the proper function of the automated image acquisition.
Select ‘Start’ to begin automated imaging.
Adjust the total laser output power as needed to ensure optimal image quality during image acquisition.
Reduce laser output for conventional image acquisition if necessary.
Increase laser output power to achieve sufficient density at the sample plane (1–3 kW/cm2) for STORM movie acquisition.
Process images to generate 3D volumes.
Identify single molecule positions within STORM movies using single-molecule fitting software.
Generate STORM image files using the identified single molecule positions and emitter PSF information.
Correct for drift that occurs during STORM image acquisition.
Download and install “STORMpro” custom GUI for volumetric STORM image processing.
Download and Install FIJI (Schindelin et al., 2012).
Download FIJI Z-align macros from the specified GitHub repository.
Install FIJI Z-align macros and XML files.
Open STORMpro and set the path to the data for analysis.
Load a .dax STORM file into the visualizer for interactive visualization.
Select all appropriate “STORM channels” corresponding to collected data.
Choose the appropriate “Alignment channel” for Z-section alignment.
Set an appropriate number of processes for concurrent fitting analysis based on computational threads available.
Set 3D-DAOSTORM fitting parameters and test fit quality using multichannel XML files.
Adjust start/end frames in the corresponding channel of the selected .dax file.
Select typically 10–20 frames in the middle or near the end of the STORM movie for analysis.
Manually input desired values for 3D-DAOSTORM SMLM fitting parameters (e.g., frame range, background, sigma, drift correction).
Save XMLs to save selected parameters to the XML directory.
Set “Movie for fitting evaluation” to the desired .dax file for analysis.
Select “Fit Parameters" to run test fits on the chosen .dax movie.
Load the output .hdf5 single-molecule localization list by dragging/dropping into the visualizer or selecting “Load localization 1”.
Inspect fit quality by visualizing fit beacons (green circles) in Figures.
Based on the fit quality, repeat steps to adjust and optimize fitting parameters.
Inspect raw .dax STORM movies in renderer software.
Determine the frame range for full .dax file single molecule fitting.
Select “Set Frame Range” and enter the start and end frames for analysis.
Input rigid registration parameters when the first FIJI subprocess launches to continue alignment.
Drag cursor within the displayed image to set a sample ROI for cropping the image stack.
Release the cursor to identify the ROI.
Close the window and press “Escape” on the keyboard to crop the dataset.
Input elastic registration parameters when the second FIJI subprocess launches to continue alignment.
